A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flexora. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison after matching pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations in Tables 1–4, alongside loss analyses, numerical smoothness experiments, and case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds a training-duration ablation in Table 5 and Qwen2.5-32B evaluations in Table 10.

M1.justification: The HPO formulation, continuous relaxation, optimization procedure, positive-hyperparameter layer selection, and retraining of selected adapters remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Algorithm 1. The appendix adaptations are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, and RACE-mid/high, with supplementary BoolQ, ARC-e, ARC-c, and OBQA comparisons. The added experiments reuse existing tasks; Qwen2.5-32B expands model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing main and appendix comparisons is unchanged. The added four-epoch LoRA control changes the training budget of an existing method, while the Qwen2.5-32B evaluation retains the LoRA-versus-Flexora comparison.

E3.justification: v4 adds a four-epoch LoRA control alongside three-epoch LoRA and Flexora with one selection epoch plus three fine-tuning epochs. It also adds evaluation on Qwen2.5-32B beyond the previous 6–8B models. Existing splits, metrics, and settings remain unchanged; Flexora's 1+3 schedule was already documented in v3.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds an ablation testing whether an additional training epoch explains Flexora's advantage. Earlier analyses of layer selection, ranks, search samples, optimization hyperparameters, losses, smoothness, and individual cases are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised. Existing random-layer comparisons and statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports four-epoch LoRA accuracy averaging 82.45%, versus the retained Flexora average of 86.46%. Table 10 adds Qwen2.5-32B averages of 83.82% for LoRA and 87.90% for Flexora. Table 5 also introduces an inconsistent three-epoch LoRA average of 82.32%: its listed scores average 82.44%, as reported in v3 Table 16 and retained v4 Table 17. Thus its stated 0.13-point epoch benefit is 0.01 using the listed scores. Existing result entries otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, Propositions 1–2, Theorem 1, and associated assumptions, equations, proofs, and derivations in Section 6 and Appendices A and E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: automatic LoRA layer selection through HPO and unrolled differentiation, improved performance and efficiency, and theoretical support. The conclusion is reworded without changing these claims.

C2.justification: The new ablation discussion explicitly attributes the advantage to layer selection rather than additional training epochs and interprets the small LoRA change as convergence by epoch three. Existing overfitting explanations, applicability qualifications, and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The new ablation documents the four-epoch LoRA control's training budget. Flexora's one-epoch selection and three-epoch fine-tuning schedule was already disclosed in v3 Table 6. Existing implementation, hardware, and configuration information is retained, but no Qwen2.5-32B-specific settings are added to Appendix B.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to previous research remain unchanged. The existing Hardt et al. (2016) reference gains conference and page details, which is bibliographic maintenance rather than a new citation.

P1.justification: v4 adds a limited ablation discussion, lightly rewrites the conclusion, and updates author-name, affiliation, and contact text. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 5 and extends v3 Table 9, now Table 10, with Qwen2.5-32B rows. These additions cause local reflow and subsequent table renumbering. Existing figures and other table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The added training-duration control addresses an alternative explanation that v3 did not directly test, and Qwen2.5-32B provides evidence at a larger model scale. These are useful but limited gains. Table 5's inconsistent average weakens numerical precision, and the missing model-specific settings limit reproducibility of the larger-model results. Nevertheless, the listed per-task results retain a clear advantage over four-epoch LoRA, so the additional comparative evidence supports a modest net improvement.
